### Observed differences

- In the earlier window, the outgoing transitions of activity A38 went mainly to A39 (about 58 in 100 observed transitions) and to A35 (about 36 in 100), with only marginal shares (about 1 in 100 each) to A23, A24, A31, A44, A45 and A12. In the later window, A35 became the most frequent successor (about 54 in 100) while A39 dropped to about 41 in 100, and small transitions to A06 (about 2 in 100) and to A20, A40 and A42 (about 1 in 100 each) appeared, while the earlier minor successors no longer show in the profile. The profile rests on 108 observed outgoing transitions before and 100 after. [DIR001]
- This routing-profile difference is larger than about 995 in 1000 random re-splits of the pooled traces, so it stands out for a single indicator; however, it is the only item that qualified across the 97 tested control-flow units, whereas about 0.48 items (roughly one in two) would be expected to qualify by chance if nothing had changed. [DIR001]

### Inference

Support level: Insufficient evidence

The evidence is insufficient to infer a change in the process. Only one control-flow item qualified where fewer than one would be expected by chance in an unchanged process, which is what a stable process typically produces, so the apparent shift of A38's transitions from A39 towards A35 as dominant successor cannot be distinguished from sampling variation between the two windows. [DIR001]

- 200 traces before, 200 traces after

- Source activity A38, outgoing transition shares
- Before: A39 got ~58% of outgoing transitions, A35 ~36%, and small shares to A23, A45, A24, A44, A12, A31 (~0.9% each)
- After: A35 got ~54%, A39 ~41%, small shares to A06 (2%), A42 (1%), A40 (1%), A20 (1%)
- Main change: A35 up ~18 percentage points, A39 down ~17 percentage points
- observed_change: 0.068 (cosine dissimilarity)
- empirical_strength: 0.995 (99.5% of reference comparisons had smaller difference)
- support: 108 outgoing transitions observed before, 100 after

Key judgement: The screening comparison. Control flow family: 1 item found vs 0.48 expected by chance. Per the instructions: "A count of the same order as that expectation (for example one or two items when fewer than one is expected) is what an unchanged process typically produces: choose 'Insufficient evidence', however large or unusual a single item looks."

So 1 item vs 0.48 expected — this is exactly the case described: one or two items when fewer than one is expected. Therefore: Insufficient evidence.

Even though the DIR001 item looks interesting (empirical_strength 0.995, a shift from A39 to A35 as the dominant successor of A38), the screening comparison dictates insufficient evidence. The instruction is explicit: "choose 'Insufficient evidence', however large or unusual a single item looks."

Based on 108 observed outgoing transitions before and 100 after. The difference is unusual for random re-splits (larger than about 995 in 1000 reference comparisons), but this is a single item.

Also note: only one item qualified across 97 tested units, while about 0.48 would be expected by chance if nothing changed.
